contents.name: Definition 3.2.1; projective implies flat and Q nonprojective
Exercise 3.2.2 (kernel of an epimorphism of flat modules)
Definition 3.2.3 and Proposition 3.2.4 (character dual and ideal tests)
Finite presentation; Exercise 3.2.5
contents.reason: Finite-presentation independence belongs with finite module presentations; preserve this prerequisite for the finitely presented flat-projective theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 3.2.6 (evaluation duality)
contents.reason: The finite-presentation evaluation isomorphism supplies the duality proof of flat-projective equivalence and is not needed for the all-modules Tor criterion.

contents.name: Theorem 3.2.7 (finitely presented flat modules are projective)
contents.reason: This finite-presentation boundary belongs to the earlier flatness development; unrestricted flat implies projective remains false here.

contents.name: Flat Resolution Lemma 3.2.8, complete induction proof
Proposition 3.2.9; Corollary 3.2.10 (flat base change)
contents.reason: Changing scalar rings requires handed bimodule tensor identities and projective base change; retain these results for the change-of-rings and Grothendieck computations.

contents.name: Lemma 3.2.11; Corollary 3.2.12 (central scalar action)
contents.reason: The central scalar-action and quotient-ring action checks must precede change-of-rings formulas; they are not assumed merely from balance in Ab.

contents.name: Corollary 3.2.13 (localization detects Tor vanishing)
contents.reason: Local detection of Tor uses flat base change and the commutative module localization criterion; retain the theorem with those hypotheses for the scalar-change sequel.

contents.name: Theorem 3.2.2 (general central localization over a noncommutative ring)
contents.reason: Retain the full theorem: a central multiplicative set S in an arbitrary unital R gives an R-flat central localization S^{-1}R. The owned example uses commutative localization only. A local construction of noncommutative central fractions and its identification with the filtered diagram of copies of R must be assigned before this additional generality can be consumed; it is not claimed proved by the commutative supplier.

Example 4.1.4, field and integer cases; fd≤pd
Proposition 4.1.5; Exercise 4.1.1 (noetherian dimension equality)
contents.reason: The finitely generated flat/projective equality and noetherian ring equality require finite presentation machinery; retain these stronger ring hypotheses in the homological commutative algebra sequel.

contents.name: pd Lemma 4.1.6; id Lemma 4.1.8; Lemma 4.1.11; global dimension proof
contents.reason: These Ext and Baer-criterion proofs supply the preceding dimension theory; this dispatch does not silently rebuild that pair.

contents.name: Example 4.1.9 (injective dimension of Z/p over Z/p²)
contents.reason: This is an injective-resolution example belonging to the Yoneda companion, independently of the Tor flat-dimension demonstration.

sources.locator: Exercise 5.1.3; §5.2 through Exercises 5.2.1–2; §5.4; §5.5 through Example 5.5.4, pp.121–124,131–136

contents.name: Exercises 5.2.1–5.2.2 (two columns and two rows)
contents.reason: The two-line exact sequences extend the five-term edge calculation and are retained for the sequel applications; general collapse is not silently substituted for them.

contents.name: Definition 5.4.4, completeness; Addendum 5.4.5
contents.reason: Completion and invariance of pages under completion need inverse-limit existence and are assigned to the explicit infinite-convergence sequel.

contents.name: Construction 5.4.6 (approximate cycles, graded Z and B)
Exercises 5.4.1–5.4.2 (completion, exhaustive/Hausdorff replacements)
contents.reason: These verify the infinite filtration invariances and belong with completion hypotheses; no such invariant is used to infer bounded homology convergence here.

contents.name: Exercise 5.4.3 (décalage)
contents.reason: Décalage shifts the filtration by chain degree and changes page number; ordinary constant filtration and complex shifts on this page do not replace that theorem.

contents.name: Exercise 5.4.4 (filtered cones)
contents.reason: The filtered-cone page comparison is retained for the double-complex and convergence sequel, which has the relevant comparison applications.

contents.name: Multiplicative Structure 5.4.8
contents.reason: Filtered differential graded algebras need product filtrations and derivation signs; multiplicative convergence belongs with the sequel applications.

contents.name: Classical Convergence Theorem 5.5.1, bounded case and proof
Classical Convergence Theorem 5.5.1, bounded-below exhaustive case
contents.reason: The unbounded exhaustive case needs colimit exactness in the ambient category and is retained for the next convergence page, not claimed for an arbitrary abelian category here.

contents.name: Example 5.5.4 (2-adic ×3 complex)
contents.reason: This exhaustiveness/Hausdorff counterexample invalidates the old CC convergence shortcut and must be included in the convergence-sequel warnings.
